issues.body: `_ESCAPABLE_NESTS` remains `(ast.If, ast.For)`, and `_exits_to_enclosing_list` returns true for a binding that is the sole statement in either nest because there are no trailing statements to reject. Thus `if repo: targets = starvation_park_targets(...); for target in targets: park_starved_partition_holder(...)` still certifies even though the loop can be reached when `repo` is false and the binding did not run. Likewise, a binding inside `for _ in items:` followed by the parking loop still certifies even though `items` may be empty. None of the new `path` or `flow` rows tests either shape: the guarded-binding row adds a trailing `return`, which exercises exit flow only after the arm has been entered, not whether the arm must be entered. Leg 4 therefore also cannot demonstrate detection of the prior counterexamples.
issues.fix_hint: Require proof that every path reaching the later statement list necessarily executes the nested binding; successful exit after an `if` arm or `for` body is insufficient. Add refused rows for a sole binding under a runtime `if` followed by the parking loop and for a sole binding inside a possibly-empty runtime `for` followed by the loop. Add a non-vacuity stand-in/mutation that makes those exact rows certify while unrelated rows keep their expected verdicts.
issues.title: Escapable nests still do not establish universal dominance

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-four dominance defect remains. The pairing still treats an ordinary `if` arm and a possibly-empty `for` body as escapable without proving that every execution reaching the later parking loop entered that arm/body. The newly added rows cover opposite arms, ordering, and an entered guard that returns, but still omit the two exact universal-dominance counterexamples from the prior review. This is materially the same major finding at the same severity, so progress is stagnant.
